Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: São Tomé and Príncipe has a general personal data protection law: Law No. 03/2016 on Protection of Personal Data, establishing ANPDP and regulating processing/transfer of personal data; no evidence found of payment-specific data provisions ([Data Protection Africa fact sheet](https://dataprotection.africa/sao-tome-and-principe/);[Law Gratis overview](https://www.lawgratis.com/blog-detail/cyber-law-at-sao-tome-and-principe-1)).
revision_notes: Both cited sources fetched and confirmed accurate and current. Law No. 03/2016 (Protection of Personal Data, enacted 10 May 2016) establishes the ANPDP and governs collection, processing, storage, cross-border transfer and notification of personal data generally; a related Law No. 07/2017 governs ANPDP's organisation. Cross-checked against RIPD (Red Iberoamericana de Protección de Datos) legislation registry, which confirms the same law is the country's operative data protection statute. No sector-specific provisions for payment transaction data were found in any source, so this is general (not payment-specific) legislation. Score of 2 (General Data Protection Legislation) is correctly calibrated against the scale and is confirmed.
revised_comments: São Tomé and Príncipe has a general personal data protection law, Law No. 03/2016 on the Protection of Personal Data, enacted 10 May 2016, which establishes the National Data Protection Agency (Agência Nacional de Protecção de Dados Pessoais, ANPDP) and regulates the collection, processing, storage, cross-border transfer and security of personal data. The law applies broadly to personal data across sectors, including data processed by payment service providers, but contains no provisions specific to payment transaction data.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: UNCDF reports very low DFS usage and cites BCSTP NFIS demand-side survey (2017) with only ~24% financial inclusion and low usage of electronic channels (ATM/debit card/internet banking = 23% of transaction volume; bank transfers via DFS = 3%; business payments via digital = 1%), implying active digital payment users are likely <20% ([UNCDF Payment Infrastructure Assessment](https://migrantmoney.uncdf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Payment-Infrastructure-Assessment-SaoTome-April2025.pdf)).
revision_notes: Cited UNCDF report fetched and confirmed: it is a 2025 UNCDF/ECCAS payment infrastructure assessment for São Tomé and Príncipe whose underlying data reflects the period up to September 2023, drawing on the BCSTP National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) demand-side survey from 2017 showing very low use of electronic payment channels. A supplementary check of the World Bank Global Financial Inclusion (Global Findex) databank corroborates extremely low digital payment activity in São Tomé and Príncipe, with only 0.9% of adults reported as using a mobile phone or the internet to access an account and 6.1% of account holders doing so — both far below the 20% threshold. No fresher or more authoritative country-specific figure was found. The evidence consistently and clearly supports the <20% band; score of 1 is confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Digital payment usage in São Tomé and Príncipe remains very low. The most recent assessment, a 2025 UNCDF/ECCAS payment infrastructure report drawing on Central Bank (BCSTP) financial inclusion survey data, finds financial inclusion at around 24% and minimal use of electronic payment channels, with active digital payment users almost certainly below 20% of the adult population. This is corroborated by World Bank Global Findex data showing under 10% of adults using a mobile phone or the internet to access a financial account.
